title: Open WebUI Vega chart rendering -- T1190 unrestricted resource loader issues attacker-chosen GETs
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70480 (GHSA-rffm-9q57-q649),
affecting Open WebUI from 0.6.34 until 0.11.0.

Open WebUI renders `vega` and `vega-lite` fenced code blocks in chat
content by building a live Vega view directly in the VIEWER's browser,
without a restricted resource loader -- Vega's own spec format supports
data-loading directives that fetch external URLs as part of rendering
the chart. Any user who can place such a block where another user will
see it (a shared chat, a channel) can make that OTHER user's browser
issue attacker-chosen outbound GET requests and have the responses from
same-origin or CORS-permissive targets rendered directly into the page
the victim is viewing -- a stored, victim-executed SSRF/data-exfiltration
primitive delivered through ordinary chat content.

Detection logic flags a stored chat message containing a `vega`/
`vega-lite` fenced code block whose spec references a `data`/`url`
directive targeting a private, loopback, or link-local address --
ordinary chart specs reference public data sources or inline data, not
internal network targets.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact fix commit and PR), fixed in 0.11.0.
